newsitem.title: ITALY: Numbers, locations for Italian-led Albania force.
newsitem.headline: Numbers, locations for Italian-led Albania force.

text.p: Nearly 1,200 soldiers from France, Italy and Spain will land in Albania on Tuesday at the start of Operation Alba (sunrise), the Italian-led security mission to the anarchic Balkan state.
Italy says the force will number 6,000 troops from eight nations once deployment is complete, with up to 2,500 in place by April 25 and the remainder joining them over the subsequent 10 days.

The key bridgeheads for the operation are the capital Tirana and the ports of Durres and Vlore. As the operation unfolds, troops will also deploy to Shkoder, Lezhe, Shengjin, Elbasan, Fier, Gjirokaster and Sarande.
Following is a breakdown of contributing nations and numbers, and a guide to where national contigents will deploy, according to an Italian briefing document for the media.

ITALY - 2,500 soldiers including mechanised infantry units, paratroops, marines, light armoured forces, logistics and communications specialists, combat and transport helicopters and naval patrol and transport vessels. The Italians will be based in the capital Tirana and in Fier and the southern port of Vlore.
FRANCE - 1,000 soldiers consisting of a mechanised regiment, helicopter units and logistics specialists. The French will be based in the port of Durres, west of the capital.
GREECE - Around 800 soldiers from a mechanised infantry battalion. The Greeks will cover an area south of Tirana as well as the town of Elbasan and have a company of troops in Vlore.
TURKEY - 600-800 marines. The Turkish area of operations will be north of Tirana and along the route from Tirana to Lezhe.
SPAIN - 450 soldiers from a mechanised infantry battalion. The Spanish will establish a presence in Lezhe and Shengjin.
ROMANIA - 400 soldiers from a mechanised infantry battalion, based in Gjirokaster.
AUSTRIA - 120 infantry soldiers, based with the Italians in Tirana.
DENMARK - 60 soldiers from a light infantry company, based with the French in Durres.
